title: Triangulation of intrinsic constructible cohomology in the site coefficient universe
statement: For a scheme T:Scheme u and finite commutative ring A:Type (u+1), the property on D(Mod of the constant A ring sheaf) that every cohomology module sheaf is intrinsically constructible is closed under isomorphisms and is triangulated. There is no cohomological boundedness condition and no completion, tower, or etale-origin condition.

source.place: ## Proof: implicit triangulation needed for the constructible restriction; agent supplement. Stacks Tag 09C3, proetale.tex, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, supplies contextual local models, not this tower-category closure theorem.

proof.text: Prove isomorphism closure by transporting every local trivialization. For zero choose one whole stratum, including for the empty scheme, the top covering sieve, and the zero finite module. Inverse image and constant module sheafification preserve zero, and restriction preserves zero morphisms. Apply the abelian exact-closure theorem. Kernel and cokernel universal-property isomorphisms transfer its selected-limit statements to the ObjectProperty closure classes. The derived homologyProperty instances then give isomorphism closure and triangulation, with no boundedness assumption.

proof_origin.place: The parent triangulation supplement; analytic part separated from the formal triangulated-category argument.
